q: How do I read a 3D NIfTI image into a NeuroVol?
a: Use neuroim2::read_vol() with the file path. It returns a NeuroVol carrying the image data and its NeuroSpace (dimensions, spacing, origin and affine); pass index to pick one volume from a 4D file.

q: How do I read a 4D fMRI NIfTI file into a NeuroVec?
a: Use neuroim2::read_vec() with the file path. It returns a NeuroVec (x, y, z, time). mode = "mmap" or "filebacked" avoids loading large files into memory; note that these two modes ignore `mask`. To read only in-mask voxels, pass `mask` with mode = "normal" (the default) or "bigvec", which requires a mask.
recipe:
vec <- neuroim2::read_vec("bold.nii.gz")
dim(vec)
ts <- neuroim2::series(vec, 30L, 30L, 20L)
# masked read (normal or bigvec mode only):
mvec <- neuroim2::read_vec("bold.nii.gz", mask = brain_mask)

q: How do I create a NeuroVol from an array and a NeuroSpace?
a: Build a NeuroSpace with the dimensions and voxel spacing, then call neuroim2::NeuroVol(data, space). The result is a DenseNeuroVol that keeps the array and its spatial reference together.
recipe:
sp <- neuroim2::NeuroSpace(c(64L, 64L, 40L), spacing = c(2, 2, 2))
vol <- neuroim2::NeuroVol(array(rnorm(64 * 64 * 40), c(64, 64, 40)), sp)
vol

q: How do I create a 4D NeuroVec from an array or a voxels-by-time matrix?
a: Call neuroim2::NeuroVec(data, space) with a 4D NeuroSpace. data may be a 4D array, or a matrix with a mask giving the in-mask voxels; the result is a NeuroVec from which series() extracts voxel time courses.
recipe:
sp <- neuroim2::NeuroSpace(c(10L, 10L, 10L, 50L))
vec <- neuroim2::NeuroVec(array(rnorm(10 * 10 * 10 * 50), c(10, 10, 10, 50)), sp)
neuroim2::series(vec, 5L, 5L, 5L)

q: How do I summarise a NeuroVec into parcel (cluster) time series?
a: Given a ClusteredNeuroVol of parcel labels, call neuroim2::ClusteredNeuroVec(vec, cvol, FUN = mean). It stores one summary time series per cluster, which is far smaller than the voxelwise data and is the usual input to parcel-level analyses.
recipe:
cvec <- neuroim2::ClusteredNeuroVec(vec, cvol, FUN = mean)
dim(cvec)
